title: Investigating Whether SAE Features Are Layer-Specific or Cross-Layer: The Portability Failure

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible: understanding feature portability informs how to interpret layer-by-layer SAE analyses. Gap between this finding and a direct safety application.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training 3 SAEs from scratch (layers 3, 6, 9), computing cross-SAE cosine similarities for all feature pairs, and manual/automated label inspection. Training alone exceeds beginner scope.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined comparison but training 3 SAEs plus the cross-layer matching and label inspection is a sustained effort project.

novelty.reasoning: This question has been largely addressed. Anthropic's crosscoders work directly studies cross-layer feature portability and introduces an architecture to resolve it. Group-SAE and RouteSAE both demonstrate and exploit cross-layer feature transferability. The proposed study of training separate per-layer SAEs and comparing features would reproduce a finding that motivated the crosscoders work.

evidence.finding: Crosscoders read and write to multiple layers simultaneously, producing shared features across layers and resolving cross-layer superposition. Directly studies feature portability across layers.
Demonstrates transferability of SAE features within different layers of a single model, enabling efficient cross-layer training.
Integrates a router with a shared SAE to dynamically extract multi-layer features, showing features can be shared across layers with proper architecture.
